channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Expand Economic Partnership, Trade Volume Increases
item.description: Euronews Serbia reports a new phase in economic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia, with trade volume increasing nearly ninefold since 2016. Uzbekistan sees Serbia as a gateway to European markets, while Serbia views it as a platform for Central Asian markets. Priorities include machinery, pharmaceuticals, and energy.

item.title: Uzbek students rank 48th out of 91 countries in PISA 2025 natural sciences
item.description: Uzbek students ranked 48th out of 91 countries in the PISA 2025 natural sciences assessment. This marks Uzbekistan's second participation in the international study, with 15-year-old students from 233 randomly selected schools participating.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks 48th in PISA 2025 natural sciences assessment
item.description: Uzbekistan participated for the second time in the PISA 2025 international assessment, with 8,652 15-year-old students from 233 schools. Students scored 438 points in natural sciences, ranking 48th out of 91 participating countries and education systems. This is an improvement from the 2022 assessment, where Uzbekistan ranked 80th with 355 points. Results for mathematics and reading are pending further analysis due to inconsistencies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Education outlines school reform progress
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Education is implementing a significant reform of its school system. The Kyrgyz Academy of Education has revised preschool and school education standards, developing clear subject standards for teachers. Funding for educational publishing has increased, with new textbooks, workbooks, and digital materials being developed. Teacher training programs are also being revised, including the introduction of dual education and continuous professional development.

item.title: Bishkek police seize synthetic drugs hidden in a water pump
item.description: Two suspects were detained in Bishkek after receiving a gasoline-powered water pump containing hidden psychotropic substances. The drugs were discovered during a special operation in June 2026. The seized substances had an estimated street value of over 1.5 million soms, preventing the distribution of over 1,700 doses.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament committee approves Malik Bekturganov as Prosecutor General candidate
item.description: A committee of the Jogorku Kenesh has approved Malik Bekturganov's candidacy for Prosecutor General. Deputies urged the new Prosecutor General to promptly address citizens' complaints and suggested opening a representative office in Russia to resolve issues for Kyrgyz citizens abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan to attract private investors to major universities and medical centers
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to gradually commercialize major higher education institutions and specialized medical centers by converting them into business entities. Private investors will be attracted by offering shares in their charter capital through public auctions, as outlined in a presidential decree.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks among top gold-buying nations this year
item.description: Uzbekistan has entered the top three countries that purchased the most gold this year. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan increased its gold reserves by 40 tons since the beginning of the year. Poland and China lead in precious metal purchases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Energy Ministry orders timely completion of winter preparation works
item.description: The Energy Minister of Kyrgyzstan has instructed heads of energy organizations to ensure timely and quality preparation of facilities for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter season. Planned repair, reconstruction, and modernization works must be completed within the set deadlines.

item.title: Criminal case on hemodialysis services violations transferred to GKNB
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office has initiated a criminal case regarding violations in hemodialysis services, transferring it to the State Committee for National Security (GKNB). The investigation is ongoing. Previous findings indicated multi-million som violations, including billing for deceased or absent patients.

item.title: Russian drone and missile strikes on Kyiv kill two, injure ten; London announces new aid package
item.description: Russian forces launched drone and missile attacks on Kyiv on September 8, resulting in two deaths and ten injuries, according to Ukrainian authorities. Damage and fires occurred in at least five districts. London announced a new aid package for Ukraine.

item.title: Vast Resources acquires 49% stake in Tajikistan's Aprelevka joint venture
item.description: Vast Resources plc has completed a reverse takeover of Gulf International Minerals Limited, acquiring a 49% beneficial interest in the Aprelevka joint venture in northern Tajikistan. The company considers this deal one of the largest foreign investments in Tajikistan's mining sector. Vast Resources' shares resumed trading on the London Stock Exchange with a market capitalization of approximately £102.9 million.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia to negotiate free trade agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia plan to begin negotiations on a free trade agreement, following the first meeting of their intergovernmental commission on economic cooperation in Belgrade. The current trade volume does not fully match the economic potential of both countries. They also aim to develop joint production and explore cooperation in sectors like manufacturing, agriculture, and IT.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament committee approves Malek Bekturganov as Prosecutor General
item.description: A committee of the Kyrgyz Parliament has approved Malek Bekturganov's candidacy for the position of Prosecutor General. Bekturganov currently serves as acting Prosecutor General. Deputies urged him to promptly address citizens' complaints and to establish a representative office in Russia for citizens abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Privatize 18 Markets and Trade Complexes, Accelerate Sales in Tashkent
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to privatize state shares in 18 markets, trade complexes, and auto markets across five regions. A presidential decree also aims to accelerate the privatization of 15 existing markets and trade complexes in Tashkent, with proceeds directed to local budgets.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans China Rail Link for Eurasian Connectivity
item.description: Tajikistan is planning a direct railway from China, potentially extending through Afghanistan and Iran to the Persian Gulf, or via Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan to Southern Caucasus and Europe. This project aims to connect Tajikistan to global ports and transform it into a central Eurasian hub.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Privatize Major State Assets Including Turonbank and Humo Air by 2026-2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to privatize major state assets, including Turonbank, Humo Air, and Uzexpomarkaz, between 2026 and 2027, according to a presidential decree. Other entities slated for privatization include Humo Air airline, the Andijan Mechanical Plant, and various markets.

item.title: Tajikistan's Glaciers Melting Rapidly, Hydrometeorology Agency Experts Report
item.description: Experts from the Hydrometeorology Agency state that Tajikistan's glaciers are melting at a rapid pace. The volume and area of the largest glacier, 'Tajikistan,' have reportedly changed.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Lower Judicial Candidate Age Limit to 30 from 35
item.description: A draft law in Uzbekistan proposes lowering the age requirement for judicial candidates from 35 to 30. The bill also suggests appointing judges for an initial five-year term, followed by a lifetime appointment.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Retain Special Rights in Privatized Strategic Companies
item.description: Uzbekistan may retain special rights to participate in the activities of strategic companies after their privatization. This mechanism aims to protect national security, economic stability, and public interests.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sentenced Over 11,700 People to Imprisonment in First Half of Year
item.description: In the first half of the year, Uzbekistan sentenced 11,703 people to imprisonment, a 23% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Fraud was the most common charge with 7,508 convictions, followed by drug offenses (5,788) and theft (4,490). Two individuals received life sentences.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan border security operation 'Tilekteshtik-2026' underway in Batken
item.description: The 'Tilekteshtik-2026' border operation, aimed at ensuring state border security and strengthening inter-agency cooperation, has entered its main phase in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region. Security units have been deployed to designated areas after showcasing specialized equipment and vehicles.

item.title: Licenses of Kyrgyz medical universities without state accreditation suspended
item.description: Licenses for medical universities in Kyrgyzstan that have not undergone state accreditation have been suspended, according to the Ministry of Health. Students have been reassigned to accredited institutions, and a timeline for potential re-accreditation remains unknown.

item.title: Liquefied gas worth 220.3 million soms embezzled in Karakalpakstan
item.description: Officials from 'Amudaryotumangaz' in Karakalpakstan allegedly embezzled liquefied gas worth 220.3 million soms by using the names of 171 citizens. Separately, officials from 'Nurobodtumangaz' misappropriated 148.3 million soms from liquefied gas sales.

item.title: Tajikistan ranks 47th globally in Global Peace Index, improving over decade
item.description: Tajikistan secured 47th place in the 2026 Global Peace Index with 1.799 points, becoming the third most peaceful Central Asian nation. Uzbekistan ranked 37th, and Kazakhstan 44th. All five Central Asian countries are in the upper half of the global ranking, with Kyrgyzstan at 61st and Turkmenistan at 66th. Tajikistan's score has improved significantly over the past ten years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to develop state program for sustainable waste management
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Natural Resources is developing a state program for sustainable waste management and secondary resources. This initiative follows improvements in legislation, extended producer responsibility, and new technical regulations for landfills. The program aims to systematically change waste management approaches in the country.

item.title: Central Asian state companies plan listings on Hong Kong Stock Exchange
item.description: Several state infrastructure companies from Central Asia are planning to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEX). Kazakhstan's railway operator KTZ has already applied for an IPO. Over 100 companies from Belt and Road Initiative participating countries are already trading on HKEX.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Implements Entry Ban for Foreign Nationals Overstaying Visa-Free Period
item.description: Foreign nationals overstaying their permitted period in Kyrgyzstan will face re-entry bans proportional to their visa-free stay duration. The Cabinet of Ministers amended rules to automatically calculate stay durations. Exceptions exist for spouses and minor children of Kyrgyz citizens, who can enter once to legalize status within 30 days.

item.title: Official in Fergana Arrested for Promising District Governor Position for $210,000
item.description: An individual claiming to be an assistant to an arbitration court judge has been arrested in Fergana region for allegedly promising a citizen the position of district governor. The suspect, identified as S.A., requested $210,000 for the service and was apprehended while receiving $100,000. Criminal charges for fraud and bribery have been filed.

item.title: Man Arrested in Fergana for Promising Governor Position for $210,000
item.description: A man was arrested in Fergana for allegedly promising to secure a district governor position for $210,000. He was apprehended while receiving an initial payment of $100,000. The individual claimed he could arrange the appointment for the Uchkoprik district governor post.

item.title: Gazprom Increases Gas Exports to Central Asia by 70 Percent
item.description: Gazprom has reported a 70 percent increase in its gas exports to Central Asian countries. According to CEO Aleksey Miller, the company has observed positive results regarding the volume of gas supplied to the region's nations. Specific details on the volume increase were not provided.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Mauritius Discuss Tourism Development Ahead of Direct Flight Launch
item.description: Uzbekistan and Mauritius held a tourism dialogue in Tashkent ahead of the first direct flight between the two countries, scheduled for December 26, 2026. The new route aims to open Uzbekistan's access to the African tourism market and strengthen Tashkent's role as a transit hub. Initially, four flights are planned, with regular weekly service starting June 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan adjusts personal assistant payment for families with multiple disabled members
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, Kyrgyzstan will change how personal assistants are paid. Assistants caring for two or more disabled individuals within the same family will receive full payment for each person. This change aims to improve care quality for children and adults with disabilities requiring constant supervision.

item.title: New Justice Minister appointed in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Almaz Aiylchiev has been appointed Acting Minister of Justice in Kyrgyzstan, replacing Ayaz Bayetov who was transferred to another position. Aiylchiev currently heads the Legal Support Department and serves as Deputy Head of the Legal Support Directorate of the President and Cabinet of Ministers. His candidacy requires Zhogorku Kenesh approval.

item.title: Tajikistan hosts forum on preserving language, culture, and historical heritage
item.description: A scientific forum on "Independent Tajikistan — the connecting link of Aryan civilization" was held in Dushanbe, organized by the World Association of Tajiks and Persian-speaking Peoples "Payvand." Over 230 guests from 27 countries attended the event, which focused on preserving language, culture, and historical heritage.

item.title: Kyrgyzpharmatsiya discusses pharmaceutical product supplies from Uzbekistan in Tashkent
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan explored expanding cooperation in the pharmaceutical sector, including Uzbek product supplies to Kyrgyzstan. Representatives from both countries discussed their organizations' work and potential future interactions. Particular attention was given to increasing pharmaceutical product imports from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tightens Entry Rules for Foreigners Overstaying Visas
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will deny re-entry to foreigners who exceed their permitted stay, with the ban duration matching their visa-free period. The Cabinet of Ministers updated regulations, with an automated system calculating stay duration. Exceptions exist for spouses and children of Kyrgyz citizens.

item.title: Uzbek Builders to Participate in 200km Railway Construction in Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan Railways will participate in its first major European railway projects, constructing a 200-kilometer railway in Serbia. This agreement was reached during an intergovernmental commission meeting in Belgrade.

item.title: Removal from Social Registry Does Not Mean Poverty Reduction, Says IHMA
item.description: The IHMA Social Protection Inspectorate is conducting oversight on families removed from the social registry. The inspectorate is examining whether decisions align with established criteria and procedures. This indicates that removal from the registry does not automatically signify a reduction in poverty.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev begins official visit to Serbia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife have arrived in Belgrade for an official visit. They were met by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić and his wife at the airport. The main events, including high-level negotiations and a business forum, are scheduled for the next day, with a package of bilateral documents expected to be signed.
